Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump's rolling back Biden-era fuel economy standards for new vehicles powered
by gasoline.
The new rules were released shortly after the president rejected an Iranian proposal
to open the Strait of Hormuz, where oil shipping disruptions have sent energy prices surging.
Separately, Trump announced a plan to build a $15 billion steel mill in Iowa, which is
expected to create as many as 2,000 permanent jobs.
The Trump administration has issued mixed messages about the recent U.S.-China meetings.
A day after the ambassador to China, David Perdue, told Fox News Sunday this.
President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world.
He actually asked the presidency, would he like to buy some at one point?
Today a reporter asked President Trump about it.
To China?
To China.
You mean to Taiwan?
No, to China.
That's what he said.
I never heard of that one.
I'm not going to have to ask him.
You mean one or so?
No, they probably like to buy it, because we do make better equipment than them.
So maybe it's a good idea.
Trump says Perdue meant to say Taiwan.
Ongoing Russian drone and missiles have hit several regions in Ukraine, including the
capital, where drones kill at least two people.
NPR's Joe Annika Hisses reports Ukraine says its drones attacked oil facilities and defense
plants in Russia.
Air raid sirens go off every couple of hours in Kiev, followed by explosions.
Russian drones hit a food market on the western outskirts of the Ukrainian capital.
Drones also hit homes, gas stations, and communications facilities.
Russia also hit a commercial vessel off the coast of Odessa and apartment buildings in
northern, central, and southern Ukraine.
In a weekend video address, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russians have amped
up the production of jet-powered drones, which are hard to shoot down.
We are developing our response, Zelensky said, including several effective prototypes of
interceptors that can take down Russian jet drones.
Joe Annika Hisses, NPR News.
The plaintiff in the lawsuit was a Cornell student at the time of the incident.
The lawsuit says she was drugged and sexually assaulted by seven fraternity members in 2024.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten says the plaintiff "did not allege
that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped," in her original statement.
Van Houten says the case will now go before a grand jury.
Cornell's vice president for university relations, Kyle Kimball, says that the university supports
the decision to reopen the investigation.
The lawsuit says Cornell didn't do enough to protect the plaintiff.
The Texas U.S. Senate contest between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Tallarico is
set to shatter campaign spending records for the Lone Star State.
Most of that spending is going to advertising.
But it's unclear how much of a difference the ad blitz will make to who wins the election,
as Houston Public Media's Andrew Schneider reports.
An analysis from advertising intelligence firm Ad Impact shows that as of mid-September,
Tallarico and groups supporting him had spent more than $53 million across all media, while
Paxton and pro-Paxton super PACs spent nearly twice that.
Erica Franklin Fowler of Wesleyan University says advertising matters chiefly at the margins
of a close contest.
It's not going to take a candidate who is not otherwise a good candidate and take them
from somewhere of like 30 percent support over a victory line.
It's really in the fraction up to a couple percentage points that advertising can move
or benefit a particular candidate.
Most polls either show the two candidates statistically tied or Tallarico with a slim
lead.
I'm Andrew Schneider in Houston.
SpaceX launched its Starship into orbit for the first time.
Today, it successfully delivered the most advanced star links yet.
The trip almost didn't happen after one of Starship's engines shut down too soon.
Elon Musk's company had scheduled a 10-hour flight.
However, the company cut short the flight.
The spacecraft reentered Earth's atmosphere over the Pacific today and splashed down near
Hawaii.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.
This election season, you can streamline your news intake with up first.

stories you need to know.
